title: RMA in Salesforce: Orders Team Walkthrough

slides.heading: Processing an RMA in Salesforce
slides.sub: A click-through walkthrough for the Orders team

slides.heading: Before you start
body: This module covers the Orders team portion of the RMA process: turning a submitted request into a Return Record, a return line, a return shipping label, and a replacement Sales Order.
Two things should already be true before you touch anything:

- The request has an associated **technical support case** documenting troubleshooting. If it doesn't, the RMA will be rejected later and sent back to Draft.
- The hardware was **originally purchased through Rently**.
You'll also need the **Serial Number** or **Order Number** from the request so you can find the original order.

slides.heading: The sequence you're about to practice
body:
- **1.** Find the original order in Salesforce
- **2.** Create the Return Record and set the request type to RMA
- **3.** Add a Return Line for the item coming back
- **4.** Create the Shipment to generate the return label
- **5.** Generate the replacement Sales Order
The simulation ahead uses real screens from Salesforce. Click the correct element to move forward. If you click the wrong thing you'll get a hint and can try again.

steps.prompt: You've searched the serial number and opened the original order. Start the return.

zones.feedback: Fedex Tracking is for following a shipment that already exists. You need to create the return record first.
That marks the order's status, it doesn't start a return.
The Related tab shows records attached to this order. The return is created from the action bar at the top right.

steps.feedback: Look in the action bar at the top right of the order for the button that creates a return record.

steps.prompt: Set the request type. Open the dropdown to choose RMA.

zones.feedback: Not yet. Choose the request type first, otherwise the record is created with no type.
That closes the dialog and discards the return record.

steps.feedback: Click the dropdown under "What type of request is this?" and select RMA.

zones.feedback: That cancels the whole thing. Use Next to continue.

steps.feedback: Use the Next button at the bottom right of the dialog.

steps.prompt: The Return Record is created. Add the item that is being returned.

zones.feedback: That creates the Shipment, which generates the return label. Add the return line items first.
Careful, that starts the replacement order. The return lines come before the order.
Generate Order builds the replacement sales order, which comes later in the process.
That adds a note, not a return line.

steps.feedback: Use the New button on the Return Lines (Return) section.

steps.prompt: The product and quantity are filled in. Now enter the serial number of the item being returned.

zones.feedback: Order Net Unit Price is a different field. You want Serial Numbers.
Status is already set to New. The serial number goes in the required field on the left.

steps.feedback: Serial Numbers is the required field on the left side of the form.

steps.prompt: Per the SOP, the Requested Refund Amount on an RMA return line should be $0. Click that field.

zones.feedback: That's Order Net Unit Price. Requested Refund Amount is on the right, near the bottom.
Rejection Reason stays as None for a standard RMA.

steps.feedback: Requested Refund Amount is the required field on the right, below Rejected Date.

zones.feedback: Cancel discards everything you just entered.
Save & New opens another blank return line. Use that only if more items are coming back on this same RMA.

steps.feedback: Use the Save button at the bottom of the form.

steps.prompt: The return line is saved. Now generate the return shipping label.

zones.feedback: You've already added the return line. The shipping label comes from the Shipments section.
That's the replacement order. The return label comes first.

steps.feedback: Use the New button on the Shipments section.

steps.prompt: Last step: create the replacement Sales Order from this Return Record.

zones.feedback: Close, but use Generate Order at the top instead. It builds the order from this return record rather than starting a blank one.
Product Weights is used for shipping estimates, not for creating the order.
Edit changes fields on the return record. You need to generate the order.

steps.feedback: Use the Generate Order button in the action bar at the top right.

slides.heading: On the Shipment screen
body: When you create the Shipment, most of it is prefilled and should be left alone. Preference, Return Shipment To, Billing and Reference Information, FedEx ShipAlert, Shipment Notes and Special Services all stay as they are.

- Add a **Phone Number** under Return Shipment From, and check those details are accurate
- Enter your best estimate of **weight and value** under Packages
- **Deselect Auto Print**
- Click **Ship Now**

slides.heading: Finishing the Sales Order
body: Generating the order is not the end. Open it and verify these on the Details tab:

- **Account Name**, **Account to be Billed**, and **Account to Assign Devices**
- **Billing Address**, **Shipping Contact**, and **Shipping Address**. Double-check the zip code
- **Shipping Service**
Then add the products on the Related tab. For an RMA the product must match the original order **exactly**. If it's no longer available, use the replacement product the Warehouse team has specified.

Finally set the hardware price. Look up the client's current contract, use the community account first and the parent account if there's no contract there. If the client has no contract at all, use list price. Update **Net Unit Price** to that figure and save.

slides.heading: Setting it to Processing
body: Once everything is verified, click the **Processing** stage at the top of the order, then click **Mark as Current Status**. The order then appears in the report RevOps works.
RevOps will send it back to Draft, and Chatter you about it, if any of these are wrong:

- The Return Record has no associated troubleshooting case
- The original order is missing from the Return Record
- The unit price doesn't match
- The shipping address is badly formatted or missing, or the contact has no phone number
- The shipping price is wrong or missing
- The item is discontinued, or there isn't enough Quantity on Hand
- SaaS ended up on the Return Record
- Account Name, Account to be Billed, or Account to Assign Devices is incomplete
Shipping should be **2nd Day Air**. If it's Overnight, fulfillment needs to confirm the rate.

questions.q: Put the Orders team steps in the correct sequence.
items: Create the Return Record and select RMA
Add the Return Line for the item
Create the Shipment to get the return label
questions.feedback: Return Record, then return line, then shipment, then the replacement order.

questions.q: What Requested Refund Amount do you enter on an RMA return line?
questions.feedback: $0. The credit is decided later, after the warehouse tests the returned device.

questions.q: On the Shipment screen, which option must you deselect before shipping?
questions.feedback: Deselect Auto Print, then click Ship Now. The other sections are left as they are.

questions.q: When adding products to the replacement order, a similar product is acceptable if the original is unavailable.
questions.feedback: The product must match the original order exactly. If it's unavailable, use the specific replacement the Warehouse team has outlined.

questions.q: A client has no contract on the community account and no communities. Where do you look next for pricing?
options: The parent or main account in Salesforce
questions.feedback: Check the parent or main account. Only if there's no existing contract anywhere do you use list price.

questions.q: Which of these would cause RevOps to send the order back to Draft? (select all that apply)
options: The Return Record has no troubleshooting case
The shipping contact has no phone number
SaaS is on the Return Record
questions.feedback: Number of properties is irrelevant. The others are all documented rejection reasons.

questions.q: After verifying the order, how do you hand it off to RevOps?
options: Click the Processing stage, then Mark as Current Status
questions.feedback: Setting it to Processing puts it in the All Orders to be Activated report. Only RevOps sets Activated.

questions.q: Which shipping service should the order use in normal circumstances?
questions.feedback: 2nd Day Air. Overnight requires fulfillment to confirm the rate.
